Resolved on current bytes: objective o1 contrasts all-address 8080:80 with loopback 127.0.0.1:8080:80, identifies the exposure boundary, and defaults development to loopback; intake lines 179 and 198 carry the rule into the lab and FT21 project.

Resolved on current bytes: objective o2 treats redaction as best effort rather than a permission boundary, prohibits printing secrets, requires add-mask for other sensitive values, and preserves the fork/GITHUB_TOKEN exception; intake line 181 applies the same rule to examples.

Resolved on current bytes: objective o2 names HTTPX and Spring RestClient, asks learners to compare explicit connect/read budgets with documented defaults and deliberately disabled timeouts, and the compatibility baseline at intake lines 288-290 names Spring Boot 4.1 and HTTPX 0.28.

Resolved on current bytes: objective o3 qualifies daemonless operation to Linux, states that macOS and Windows use a Linux VM started with podman machine, and limits compatibility to the named course commands; intake line 286 preserves the OS qualification.

Resolved on the final intake bytes: lines 278-292 declare demonstrated minimums, tested status, tagged sources, and OS notes for Docker Engine/CLI, Compose, Podman, Node, Spring Boot, FastAPI, HTTPX, actions/checkout, and docker/build-push-action. Fresh GitHub API checks reconfirmed both action tag commits on 2026-10-12.

Resolved on the final intake bytes: lines 177-178 and 198 label the password as disposable local-development configuration, distinguish environment wiring from production secret protection, point to Compose secrets for production, require an env file to be ignored and untracked, and specify a public git ls-files check; line 208 teaches this before FT21 application.
